observations.text: No clear policy explaining control and mitigation measures for hazardous energy.

positives: Emergency generator started by junior officer
Emergency fire pump tested with pressure verification
style: Focuses on company policies and SMS references showing where procedures are written
Expects every checklist point to be clearly supported in the SMS
After verifying the SMS, checks the related checklist and then the corresponding PMS jobs
Instructed the C/O to remove all canvas covers from equipment for inspection
Calls crew members individually to the CCR for questioning

questions.q: What is hazardous energy, company policy and procedure?
What is company policy for testing of high level alarm?
What is company policy for testing of cargo and ballast valves?
What is company policy for changing relief valve settings?
What is company policy for Ship/Shore Safety Checklist, R checks to be carried out, and who is responsible for carrying out R checks?
Enclosed space entry procedure, specifically where the procedure for pre-checks is written?
What is company policy for testing high level alarm? Show records and PMS jobs.
Show company policy for retirement of ropes and wires, etc.
Procedure for discarding ropes and minimum rope requirement?
Show in SMS the Vent Mast protection screen requirement, change interval requirement, and related PMS jobs?
Show Ship/Shore Safety Checklist and ensure terminal side also carries out checks?
List of ESD points. Show SMS procedures for ESD testing and procedure for carrying out ESD tests?
Manifold valve timing records for closing. Company procedure mentioning minimum and maximum closing duration?
What is company policy for checking ballast and hold space sounding? Show related records?
FGDS testing - random one point tested?
Location of ESD points and how to activate them?
Under which conditions ESD should be activated?
How to test inflatable life jackets and different methods of inflation?
When to use normal life jackets and inflatable life jackets?

checks.item: MOB marker line attached to lifebuoy and not on buoyant line
Vent opening and closing status as per port requirements
Emergency generator started by junior officer
Embarkation ladder inspection including shackle and thimble condition
CO2 room inspection and release procedure
Aft towing wire and reel condition
FPK store inspection and bilge alarm
Emergency fire pump tested along with pressure verification
Compressor room entry and leak checks
Motor room checked for seal leakage

tips: Ensure every checklist point is clearly supported in the SMS
Keep PMS records and testing records readily available for high level alarms, cargo and ballast valves, and relief valves
Be prepared to show company policies for hazardous energy, ESD testing, and rope retirement
Crew should know ESD points, activation conditions, and life jacket inflation methods
summary: The inspection focused heavily on company policies and SMS references, with the inspector verifying that every checklist point was supported by written procedures and PMS records. The deck round and crew interviews covered ESD, life jackets, and various safety equipment. The main takeaway is that under SIRE 2.0, practical operation alone is not sufficient; every activity must be traceable through SMS procedures, company policies, PMS records, and crew familiarity.
